Name: John Bambrook
Question: Did Darth Vader make promoting officers while executing their predecessors a habit?
Answer: When you or I have something that breaks down usually we might try and fix it or have it repaired. Not the Empire. If something broke down or fell into disarray the Galactic Empire would more often than not have the entire object, weapon, vehicle or whatever replaced immediately. The same can be said for Darth Vader, as he wasted no time at all on incompetent, weak or foolish officers. He also used his position of power, and the radius of fear that the darkside created to instil motivation, fear and unquestionable loyalty. Vader took this stance immediately and established dominance the first time he was presented by the Emperor to the upper echelons of the Imperial military. Out with the old and inferior, and in with whoever is next in line. This grim spectacle served as motivation to the rest of Vaders men, and was done in a bid to boost performance. Their deaths would serve as a reminder of who employed them to all onlookers,..and the high standards that Vader demanded. Admiral Ozzel, Captain Needa, and other unfortunate Imperials lost their station, and were replaced by the Sith Lord. This courtesy didn't just apply to the Imperial officers, but also untold numbers of Stormtroopers and support staff. Vader used tremendous fear and an ominous, unsettling mood to convey his intentions. Like his master, and every Sith before him, he used fear, anger, and hatred to empower himself in the darkside, and create an aura of “If I stuff up while the boss is over my shoulder…I'm a dead man.” Those Imperial officers that were replaced had outworn their rank and position. They had demonstrated ineptitude in their tenure as an Imperial officer, and were given ‘early retirement’ for their services to the Empire. We may see this a couple of times in the movies, but in the Darth Vader comics the dark lord disposes of officers and troopers as if he's trying to beat a personal best; or set some kind of twisted record for how many he can execute in a day. It's not as if the Empire couldn't replace them, and the line of officers eager to prove their worth to Vader was a very long one. Once again, Vader knew that there were many other officers keen to impress him, and that by making examples out of incompetency he would set a very high standard for all his officers. Sometimes Vader executed officers for betraying him.. Fear would be their greatest motivator to ensure that they don't get looked over, especially when the next promotion was imminent. Vaders influence would produce ruthless, efficient and ‘take no s#@%’ officers that were loyal to the Empire…but more importantly loyal to Vader himself.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What if Vader somehow managed to find Luke on Tatooine a couple of years after revenge of the sith (say he sensed him through the force or something)?
Answer: If Vader ever found his son Luke, then it would mean his confrontation with Kenobi would be pushed forward, and after defeating his former master Vader would almost certainly keep Luke a very well guarded secret from the Emperor. If Vader managed to locate Luke it would also mean imminent death for Lukes aunt and uncle, Owen and Beru Lars. This would be the perfect opportunity for Vader to tie up any loose ends, by procuring his lost son, eliminating the Lars for their betrayal,..finally dealing with Kenobi….and to ultimately teach his son the ways of the darkside so that together they can overthrow Palpatine; together as father and son. After ascertaining Lukes exact location the operation would more than likely go down something like this… Darth Vader assembles an elite death squad consisting of 4 Inquisitors, several squads of Death troopers and Purge troopers, and a backup battalion of Stormtroopers sitting in orbit. He then devises an extraction method to obtain Luke, which the Inquisitors and Purge troopers will execute upon his orders. This will eliminate Owen and Beru in the process,..leaving Vader and his Deathtroopers free to crush Kenobi at their will. After the defeat of Kenobi, Vader uses the force to eliminate all witnesses to the affair, including all the Inquisitors and Imperial personnel involved, then ultimately devises a lie to present to his master. The death of Kenobi, and the consequent “battle” on Tatooine would serve as the perfect cover to whisk Luke away to a well hidden location…and to indoctrinate his son into the Sith. The Emperor would be most pleased that Vader finally killed his former Jedi Master, and could now completely focus on eradicating the last remaining Jedi…Master Yoda. Unbeknownst to Palpatine though Vader would have already begun Lukes training in secret, ala Starkiller in The Force Unleashed. Only unlike Starkiller Luke would not be viewed as expendable. Vader would harness Lukes tremendous power,…and in time the two Sith Lords would usurp the Emperors throne. Unless Master Yoda somehow intervened Princess Leia would either grow up unawares of her connection to the rulers of the galaxy, or be eliminated upon her discovery..according to the Rule of Two. Unless Luke had future aspirations to acquire his fathers throne…

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What is the most terrifying thing about Darth Vader?
Answer: He is a virtually unstoppable, long foretold prophesied “chosen one”, that can effortlessly use his mind to implode your head..and no one could stop any of this carnage and madness until he had returned balance to the force. His utter lack of humanity was absolutely terrifying, and he didn't care if he had to slaughter women and children to achieve ultimate power. He was driven by fear, yet ruled by it…and his methods were harsh, cruel and sadistic in nature. His mere presence instilled pure dread in all but a few, and he didn't even have to be on the same planet as you to kill you. I think that last one was pretty terrifying, because imagine for a moment that Vader was your boss, and you'd been using his favourite mug in the work place, or parking in his reserved spot,..or even just nodded at him in a fashion that he felt unbefitting for a Sith Lord. What then? The answer is nothing that matters; because there is nothing that you could possibly do if Vader was dead set on killing you. He could use the force to make you trip down a huge flight of stairs, or open an airlock unexpectedly blowing you into space, or wait until you began eating a meal and make it look like you choked on a piece of food. Or he could just get real shitty at you and crush your larynx from his kitchen, or the other side of the planet..or the other side of our whole star system for that fact.

Question: Did Yoda come across a Sith Lord prior to The Phantom Menace?
Answer: The first Sith Lord Yoda actually encountered was his former pupil, Count Dooku, but this happened during Attack of the Clones. By the end of The Phantom Menace Yoda and the Jedi Council had concluded that it was indeed a Sith Lord that Obi-Wan had despatched on Naboo, and Yoda was firm in believing that his master, or his apprentice, still remained hidden. During his long lifetime Yoda was canonically alive at the same time as five confirmed Sith Lords. Legends includes Darth Tenebrous and his master. Darth Tenebrous and his Twi'lek Sith Lord Master, Darth Plagueis, Darth Sidious, Darth Maul, Darth Tyranus, and Darth Vader all lived and breathed during the time Yoda was a Jedi. It was Darth Tenebrous and his master that created a rift in the force, so powerful that the darkside made itself known to every Jedi when the two performed the ritual. Although the Jedi of the time could sense the darkside, none could tell who originated the powerful rift. Plagueis was living on Sojourn before events in The Phantom Menace, and Yoda never actually met his public persona, Hego Damask. Count Dooku, Qui-Gon Jinn, Sifo Dyas and Jocasta Nu actually did though, during a diplomatic meeting with the Intergalactic Banking Clan magister. Plagueis used this meeting to undermine the Jedi, and plant the seeds of doubt in Dooku's conflicted mind. Although Plagueis had Sidious as his apprentice, Dooku was already being subtly persuaded by a Sith Lord to join the darkside..long before Darth Sidious made designs on the Serenno nobleman.

Question: Would Darth Maul be able to kill someone with the horns on his head? Would he be able to impale someone with them?
Answer: Well, Savage his brother did this exact thing to the Jedi Adi Gallia during the Clone Wars. After responding to Hondo Ohnaka at his pirate base on Florrum Adi Gallia and Obi-Wan Kenobi encounter Maul and his brother Savage. Gallia and Savage engage in combat and after holding her own against the enormous Zabrak for a short while his incredible strength and fury gets the better of the small Tholothian. Savage uses the force to send Gallia flying into the hull of a wrecked space craft, then takes a run up and impales her directly in the chest. More than likely this killed her, as her body is motionless before Savage lands his cruel killing blow. This little move of his really harks on his namesake. Maul is capable of doing the exact same thing, although it's not really his style. When Maul was languishing on Lotho Minor, after being bisected by his nemesis Kenobi, we see that his horns if left unchecked can grow much longer than we first thought. If he used the ‘Savage technique’ on someone with those gnarly horns it would definitely messy up their day. Even his horns at their typical length could do enough damage to kill or maim an opponent, but just imagine him headbutting someone in the face! So,..I think its safe to say that Maul could kill someone with the horns on his head.
